Who is bound: cl 5(1)-(2): made under s 47(1) of the Essential Services Commission Act 2001 (Vic); 'applies to, and must be complied with by, all retailers in respect of their activities in relation to small customers and exempt persons'. summary: Energy Retail Code of Practice (Victoria). Bound: cl 5(1)-(2): made under s 47(1) of the Essential Services Commission Act 2001 (Vic); 'applies to, and must be complied with by, all retailers in respect of their activities in relation to small customers and exempt persons'. Exempt persons only where a clause says so. Schedule 1 lists civil penalty requirements.

clauses.heading: Explicit informed consent
clauses.text: Consent is explicit informed consent only if the retailer, or a person acting for it, disclosed all relevant matters clearly, fully and in plain English, including each specific purpose or use, and the small customer was competent to give it.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 7(1). Victorian version adds plain English and competence. An agent that signs up a confused or apparently incapable customer, or skips disclosure, obtains no valid consent.

clauses.heading: Pre-contractual duty of retailers
clauses.text: A retailer must obtain a small customer's explicit informed consent before entering the customer into a market retail contract.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 26(4). Enrolling a Victorian customer on a market offer without explicit informed consent. Civil penalty requirement (Schedule 1).

clauses.heading: Minimum standards - customers entitled to clear advice
clauses.text: Before obtaining consent to a customer retail contract, a retailer must explain in a readily understandable way the terms under which amounts payable may vary with the customer's actions (for example conditional discounts), among other matters.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 38(1). An agent that closes a sale without explaining conditional discounts or how the retailer may change prices breaches this civil penalty requirement.

clauses.heading: Manner of advertising conditional discounts
clauses.text: When advertising a conditional discount, a retail marketer must state the conditions clearly and conspicuously, and the conditional discount must not be the most prominent price-related matter.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 48. An agent that leads with 'save 30%' without the conditions, or headlines a conditional discount, breaches cl 48 (48(1) and 48(2) are civil penalty requirements).

clauses.heading: Payment arrangements
clauses.text: A retailer must accept a residential customer's payment proposal, or revised proposal, that meets the Code's requirements.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 130(2). An agent that rejects a compliant proposal (equal payments at intervals up to one month, arrears cleared within two years, covering ongoing use, based on reasonable forecast) breaches a civil penalty requirement.

clauses.heading: Minimum assistance (tailored assistance)
clauses.text: Tailored assistance for residential customers in arrears includes repaying arrears over up to two years by regular payments, and specific advice about government and non-government assistance such as Utility Relief Grants and energy concessions.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 128(1). An agent that tells a customer in arrears they must pay in full, or omits Utility Relief Grant and concession information, denies a statutory entitlement.

clauses.heading: Retailer obligations
clauses.text: A retailer must, whenever relevant, including when a residential customer contacts it, give clear and unambiguous information about the payment difficulty assistance available, in a timely way.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 141(1)(c). An agent that fails to tell a customer who raises payment difficulty about Part 6 assistance breaches a civil penalty requirement and undermines the precondition for any later disconnection (cl 187(1)(a)).

clauses.heading: Restriction on conditions
clauses.text: A retailer must not make payment difficulty assistance conditional on the customer providing personal or financial information or waiving an entitlement under the Code.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 143(1). An agent that says 'send me your bank statements first' or 'you must give up your concession' before offering assistance breaches this civil penalty requirement.

clauses.heading: Residential customer only to be disconnected as a last resort for non-payment
clauses.text: Disconnection for non-payment is a last resort; a retailer must not arrange disconnection of a residential customer's premises where total arrears are under $1,000 (including GST).
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 187. An agent that threatens disconnection for arrears under $1,000, or before assistance obligations under cl 141 are met, misstates the law. 187(2) is a civil penalty requirement; the $1,000 figure is new in Version 7.

clauses.heading: Ongoing retailer obligations (life support)
clauses.text: Within one business day of being told of a change to life support equipment requirements or contact details, a retailer must update its register of life support customers and residents.
clauses.notes: Provision read: cl 165(1). An agent that does not capture or route a life support update, so the register is not updated within one business day, causes a civil penalty breach.
